title: 湖南省高校新生传染病认知的统计调查：HPV感染认知短板及其调节因素
creator: 李林 刘, 秀洪 袁
description: 目的高校新生是传染病健康教育的重要目标人群，提升其传染病防控知识水平对于促进校园公共卫生安全具有重要意义。了解湖南省高校新生对艾滋病(acquired immunodeficiency syndrome，AIDS)、人乳头瘤病毒(human papilloma virus，HPV)感染、乙型病毒性肝炎(以下简称“乙肝”)和肺结核(pulmonary tuberculosis，PTB)4种重要传染病的认知水平及其影响因素，重点探究学校层面特征(如学历结构、专业设置、地区)对学生传染病认知的差异化影响，为高校开展精准、有效的入学阶段健康教育提供实证依据。方法于2025年秋季学期，采用横断面调查方法，对湖南省36所高校(涵盖不同地区、层次和类型)的全体一年级新生进行匿名问卷调查。调查共回收有效问卷156 185份。问卷内容涵盖4种传染病的基础知识、传播途径及预防措施，并收集学校信息。以各题目回答正确率(比例数据)为因变量，经反正弦平方根变换后，构建线性混合效应模型进行分析。模型纳入学校所在地区、学校层次、是否设有临床医学专业、学生性别比例、本科学生比例、研究生比例及疾病类型等固定效应，并设置学校随机截距和题目随机截距(嵌套于疾病类型)以控制数据层次结构。通过比较包含交互项(重点关注本科比例、医学专业设置与疾病类型的交互)的模型与主效应模型，识别关键调节因素。结果新生对4种疾病相关知识的认知正确率总体分化显著：对AIDS(84.5%)与TB(90.6%)相关知识的认知正确率较高，而对HPV感染(55.1%)和乙肝(76.5%)相关知识的认知正确率较低，其中对HPV感染相关知识的认知正确率低于其他疾病(P<0.001)。本科比例呈现负向调节效应：学校本科学生比例对认知水平的影响因疾病类型而异；在控制其他变量后，本科比例对HPV感染和乙肝认知存在显著的负向调节作用(交互项均P<0.001)；即在本科比例较高的学校，新生对HPV感染和乙肝的认知相对于AIDS显著较低。医学专业发挥正向保护效应：学校设有临床医学专业对HPV感染认知存在显著的正向调节作用(P=0.024)；这表明，在医学专业院校，新生(包括非医学专业学生)的HPV感染相关知识的认知正确率显著优于非医学专业院校。其他因素影响有限：学校所在地区、学校层次及学生性别比例对总体相关知识的认知正确率无显著主效应或调节效应。研究生比例的影响未达到统计学意义。随机效应模型显示，学校间差异仅解释总变异的5.74%，而疾病间差异解释35.43%，表明认知差异主要源于疾病知识特性本身，高校间的教学影响在新生入学初期尚未成为主要分化来源。结论湖南省高校2025级新生对不同传染病的认知存在显著差异，其中对HPV感染相关知识的认知正确率最低。学校特征主要通过调节效应影响认知水平，本科比例较高的院校在HPV感染和乙肝认知方面相对存在劣势，而设有医学专业的高校与较高的HPV感染相关知识的认知正确率存在关联。高校新生入学阶段是开展针对性传染病健康教育的重要窗口期。高校环境因素对不同传染病认知水平的差异化调节作用，为传染病健康教育资源的精准配置提供了新的分析视角。 大学生群体作为国家未来发展的重要力量，其身心健康与社会稳定和进步息息相关。高校环境具有人口高度密集、集体生活接触频繁、人员跨地域流动性强等显著特征，这使得校园极易成为传染病传播与暴发的场所。具体而言，艾滋病(acquired immunodeficiency syndrome，AIDS)、人乳头瘤病毒(human papilloma virus，HPV)感染、乙型病毒性肝炎(以下简称“乙肝”)和肺结核(tuberculosis，TB)是当前威胁大学生群体健康的4种重点传染病。AIDS作为一种不可治愈的严重传染病，在青年学生中流行趋势严峻；HPV感染与多种癌症密切相关；病毒性肝炎可导致肝硬化、肝癌等严重后果；TB则具有高度传染性。然而，大学生群体对这些疾病的认知仍存在盲区：对传播途径存在误解(如误认为AIDS可通过日常接触传播)，对关键预防措施(如安全套使用、疫苗接种)的认知与践行不足，对疾病的隐匿性、主动检测的重要性及感染者的权益也缺乏清晰认识。这些认知不足不仅影响大学生对相关疾病风险的理解与防护，也使其在面对流感等传统传染病以及新型冠状病毒肺炎等新发传染病时面临更大的健康风险。因此，系统评估并提升大学生对传染病的认知水平、防控意识与健康相关行为能力，不仅是保障学生个体健康、维护正常教学秩序的必然要求，更是筑牢校园公共卫生安全防线、提升全社会突发公共卫生事件应对能力的战略基石[1-3]。 近年来，国内外学者围绕大学生传染病认知与防控开展了大量实证研究，普遍揭示了大学生群体传染病健康素养整体偏低的现状。大学生对传染病基本知识，如传播途径、核心症状、分类及疫苗原理等，知晓率不高，且存在显著差异。例如，师浩楠等[4]的研究发现，仅约55%的大学生会主动关注传染病常识，对甲类传染病包含种类的准确回答率不足一半。Delicati等[5]在意大利帕多瓦大学对1 059名不同专业的大学生开展了横断面调查，结果表明，医学生比非医学生对医源性感染的认知更高，个人照顾经历与新型冠状病毒肺炎疫情提升了学生对感染预防的重视，但知识差距依然存在，提示需将针对性预防教育纳入大学课程。Liou等[6-7]针对美国新泽西州立大学304名本科生的横断面调查显示，基于健康信念模型分析，女生比男生采取了更多预防新型冠状病毒肺炎感染的行为且健康信念的各维度得分更高，年长学生比年轻学生的预防行为更多且感知障碍更少，提示需针对不同群体设计干预措施以提升健康行为动机和自我效能。陈瑶等[8]在新发传染病疫情期间的调查中也指出，大学生对正确洗手、佩戴口罩等具体防护技能的知晓率仅为三至四成。这种认知短板直接影响了防护行为的依从性。研究进一步揭示了认知水平的影响因素具有多维度和不平衡性。人口学特征方面，普遍共识是女生的认知水平及行为依从性通常优于男生；医学专业学生因学科背景优势，其疾病相关的知识掌握程度、防护态度和行为实践均显著高于非医学专业学生；来自城镇、家庭社会经济地位较高(尤其母亲文化程度高)的学生往往表现出更好的健康素养。地域与环境因素亦发挥作用，如孙海峰等[9]发现济南高校农村生源学生的健康素养水平低于城市生源学生，少数民族学生低于汉族学生。此外，信息获取渠道高度依赖新媒体(如微信、微博)，但信息甄别能力不足可能带来误导风险[8]。 在干预层面，健康教育能有效提升大学生的“知信行”水平。通过健康知识科普讲座、互动教学、多媒体等多种形式结合的健康教育，能显著提升学生对传染病知识的掌握率和良好卫生习惯养成率。田鑫等[10]强调，提升“传染病健康素养”对促进正确预防行为(如咳嗽礼仪、公筷使用)具有关键作用。当前教育实践呼吁采用多元化、精准化的策略，如利用“互联网+”平台开展生动宣传、加强普及非医学生的医学常识、实施针对薄弱人群(如男生、农村生源、少数民族学生)的精准干预，并探索“医校联动”“同伴教育”等创新模式[4, 10]。国际上早已将健康素养视为个体乃至群体健康结局的核心决定因素之一，其在传染病预防控制领域的重要性在SARS、H1N1流感、埃博拉及新型冠状病毒感染等多次疫情中不断被验证和强化[11]。世界卫生组织(World Health Organization，WHO)等机构积极倡导将健康素养提升作为公共卫生干预的基础性战略。研究[12]表明，较高的健康素养能够帮助个体更好地理解疫情信息、遵从公共卫生建议、识别错误信息，从而采取有效的自我保护行为，并减轻疫情带来的心理恐慌。在国外的健康教育中，针对青年学生，尤其是大学生群体的研究，同样关注其健康素养水平及影响因素，并积极探索基于学校环境的健康促进项目。研究[13]不仅关注知识传播，更重视批判性思维培养、自我效能感提升及健康行为支持性环境的构建。这些理念与实践与国内研究倡导的“知信行”模式深化、精准化干预和多元化教育手段不谋而合，共同指向一个核心：提升以健康素养为基础的传染病综合防控能力。 综上所述，尽管国内外已有相当研究积累，但中国大学生传染病认知与防控仍面临认知基础不牢、群体差异显著、行为转化不足等挑战。湖南省作为中国的高等教育大省，拥有数量众多、类型各异的高校及庞大的在校大学生群体，这一密集且活跃的群体在校园内外构成了一个复杂而动态的公共卫生界面。然而，针对该区域大学生传染病认知水平与健康素养的系统性调查尚不充分，其认知现状、影响因素及群体内部差异(如西部和非西部高校、不同学历、不同性别)仍缺乏以本省数据为基础的精准画像。现有全国性研究虽揭示了普遍性问题，但难以直接指导具有湖南地方特色的校园健康教育实践。因此，在“健康中国”战略深入推进与后疫情时代校园常态化防控的背景下，立足于湖南省的实际情况，开展一项系统、深入的实证研究，全面评估本省大学生传染病认知与健康素养现状，并剖析其深层影响因素，对于填补地域研究空白、为省内教育及卫生部门制订精准化、差异化的校园健康促进与传染病防控干预策略，具有不可或缺的理论价值与现实紧迫性。 对象与方法 伦理声明 本研究已获得中南大学湘雅三医院医学伦理委员会批准(审批号：快26249)。 调查对象 本研究面向湖南省高等院校2025级入学新生，调查对象为湖南省36所高校2025级秋季学期首次进入当前培养阶段学习的新生群体，涵盖专科、本科及研究生不同培养层次的学生。参与高校涵盖综合类、医学类及职业院校等不同办学类型。 调查实施与质量控制 于2025年9月至10月采用方便整群抽样方法开展调查，调查主要在新生入学初期及系统性健康教育活动全面开展前实施，旨在尽可能反映学生入学阶段的基础传染病认知水平。本研究采用“问卷星”平台开展线上匿名问卷调查，由各高校统一组织实施，学生通过手机或电脑在线完成填写。调查过程中不收集姓名、学号等个人身份信息，以保障匿名性与数据真实性。为提高数据质量，问卷核心题项均设置为必答项，并对明显异常、信息不完整及答题时间过短的问卷进行筛除。问卷提交后由系统自动汇总，并在数据整理阶段进一步进行逻辑核查与数据清洗。 问卷描述 采用自编的《湖南省2025级新生传染性疾病相关知识调研问卷》进行横断面调查。问卷共分为5个部分：第1部分为一般人口学信息(就读学校、性别、就读阶段)；第2至5部分分别评估对AIDS、HPV感染、乙肝及TB共4种重点传染病的核心认知。问卷题型以单项选择题为主，在HPV感染与乙肝认知部分设置多选题，共计18个核心知识题项，上述4种传染病依次设8、4、2和4个。内容紧密围绕疾病的传播途径、关键预防措施(如安全套使用、疫苗接种)、常见误解澄清(如日常接触传播AIDS)、症状识别(如TB可疑症状)及正向态度(如主动检测、规范治疗、权益保护)等进行设计，旨在系统考察新生的知识认知准确度、误区辨识力及健康态度取向。 本问卷内容基于国家权威疾控机构发布的核心信息编制，主要用于高校新生传染病相关知识认知的现况调查。内容覆盖4种重点传染病的传播、预防及健康行为等方面，可用于初步评估高校新生相关传染病知识认知水平。本研究重点关注群体相关知识差异，因此未对问卷开展系统的测量信度和效度验证。 统计学处理 采用题目层面正确率作为认知指标。每道题目根据作答结果判定为“正确”或“错误/不知道”，认知正确率定义为某题目正确作答人数占该题目总作答人数的百分比。不同传染病的总体认知情况主要依据对应题目正确率的整体分布进行比较分析。统计方法采用单因素方差分析和t检验考察多组样本平均水平的差异；采用样本皮尔逊相关系数考察传染病和各变量之间的相关性；采用线性混合效应模型(linear mixed-effects model，LMM)分析高校新生传染病认知正确率的影响因素。由于传染病认知正确率 P 为比例数据(0~1之间)，在建模前对其进行反正弦平方根变换(arcsine square-root transformation，ASRT)，以符合模型的正态性和方差齐性假设。 模型构建 以个体的传染病认知正确率(ASRT后)为因变量。固定效应变量包括以下10个： 1)截距项：参照组为其他地区(Xi 1=0)、普通高校(Xi 2=0)、无临床医学类专业(Xi 3=0)、男生比例为0、本科比例为0、研究生比例为0的AIDS正确率。 2)考虑到湖南省高校地域、层次和专业分布的差异，为了考察这些差异对学生4种传染病认知能力的影响，本研究设置3个反应学校差异的变量：学校地域类型变量X 1(省会高校、西部高校和其他地区高校)；学校层次变量X 2(985/211/双一流高校和其他高校)、学校有无医学专业变量X 3(有临床医学专业和无临床医学专业)。变量X 1、X 2和X 3均为分类变量。对X 1的3个不同取值对应的正确率进行单因素方差分析，P<0.

title: 护士对基于AI动态评估静脉血栓栓塞风险接受度的潜在剖面分析及其影响因素
creator: 圣莉 程, 楠楠 李, 嘉 黄, 伟娜 王, 敏 方, 雪梅 詹, 文风 林, 凌云 田
description: 目的随着智慧护理的快速发展，用于动态评估静脉血栓栓塞(venous thromboembolism，VTE)风险的人工智能(artificial intelligence，AI)系统已在临床逐步推广，但护士作为该系统的直接应用者，其接受度的高低直接影响技术的临床应用效果。然而，护士对使用AI动态评估VTE风险的接受度是否存在群体异质性，目前尚不明确。本研究旨在通过潜在剖面分析(latent profile analysis，LPA)识别护士对使用AI动态评估VTE风险接受度的潜在类别，并剖析其影响因素，为制订分群、分层的推广与培训方案提供实证依据。方法采用便利抽样法，于2025年4月至6月对安徽省皖南、皖中及皖北地区三级医院的护士进行调查，采用一般资料调查表、临床护士预防住院患者VTE行为量表、护士职业态度量表、护士使用AI动态评估VTE风险接受度问卷进行调查。采用LPA识别护士使用AI动态评估VTE风险接受度的潜在类别，多元Logistic回归分析探讨各因素对不同类别的影响。结果共回收有效问卷2 323份。护士使用AI动态评估VTE风险接受度分为3个潜在剖面(3组)：低接受度-顾虑抗拒组[388例(16.8%)]；中接受度-谨慎观望组[1 177例(50.5%)]，高接受度-积极接纳组[758例(32.7%)]。护士工作年限、夜班频率、临床护士预防住院患者VTE行为量表中知识维度评分及护士职业态度量表评分是护士使用AI动态评估VTE风险接受度潜在剖面的影响因素(均P<0.05)；在控制协变量后(以低接受度-顾虑抗拒组为参照)，护士职业态度量表评分越高，归入中接受度-谨慎观望组、高接受度-积极接纳组的可能性越大，比值比(odds ratio，OR)分别为1.023、1.074(均P<0.001)；夜班频率几乎很少甚至无与夜班频率为2~3次/月的护士更倾向归入中接受度-谨慎观望组(OR=1.773、OR=2.243，均P<0.05)与高接受度-积极接纳组(OR=3.964、OR=4.300，均P<0.001)；工作年限≤5年(OR=4.942，P<0.001)及10~19年(OR=3.361，P=0.006)的护士均更倾向于归入高接受度-积极接纳组；临床护士预防住院患者VTE行为量表中知识维度评分越高的护士，越易归入高接受度-积极接纳组(OR=1.042，P=0.009)。结论护士对基于AI动态评估VTE风险的接受度存在明显的群体异质性。医院管理者应重点关注对AI动态评估VTE风险接受度为“低接受度-顾虑抗拒”和“中接受度-谨慎观望”的护士，提升其对新技术的接受水平。 国家卫生健康委员会办公厅发布的《2025年国家医疗质量安全改进目标》[1]中“提高静脉血栓栓塞(venous thromboembolism，VTE)规范预防率”已连续5年成为国家医疗质量安全十大改进目标之一。VTE作为住院患者高发且可预防的致死性并发症，其早期精准风险评估是降低发病率的首要防线。目前临床VTE风险评估主要依赖人工评估量表[2-4]，其准确性高度依赖于护士的知识水平、临床经验甚至工作状态，存在评估效率偏低、漏判与误判风险较高等问题[5]。近年来，人工智能(artificial intelligence，AI)驱动的VTE动态风险评估系统已在临床广泛应用，有效提升了VTE风险预测的准确性与时效性[6-7]。尽管AI系统在VTE风险评估中展现出显著优势，但其在临床护理实践中的落地效果高度依赖于护士的接受度，即护士认同并主动采用该技术的主观意愿[8]。护士的接受度不仅直接影响AI系统的使用效能与工作流程优化，更决定了智慧护理技术能否真正转化为临床实效。然而，目前国内关于护士对AI动态评估VTE风险接受度的研究仍较为匮乏，且现有研究大多忽略了不同特质个体之间的差异，缺乏对群体异质性的深入探讨[9]。因此，本研究基于潜在剖面分析(latent profile analysis，LPA)[10]识别护士对使用AI动态评估VTE风险接受度的潜在类别特征并深入剖析其影响因素，为医院护理管理者制订分群、分层的AI动态评估VTE风险推广与培训方案提供实证依据。 对象与方法 伦理声明 本研究已获得中国科学技术大学附属第一医院伦理委员会批准(审批号：2024KY伦审第485号)，调查对象均对本研究知情同意并自愿参与。 对象 2025年4月至6月，采用便利抽样法，选取安徽省皖南、皖中、皖北地区使用AI动态评估VTE风险的三级医院的2 500名护士为调查对象。纳入标准：1)年龄≥18岁；2)取得护士执业资格证书且工作时间≥1年；3)所在医院使用AI系统进行住院患者VTE风险动态评估的时间不少于3个月；4)近3个月内使用该系统的频率≥5次/周；5)对本研究知情同意，自愿参与。排除标准：1)调查期间不在岗(休假、外出学习等)；2)在院实习、规培、进修等。采用横断面研究样本量计算公式估算样本量，公式为n=(UαS/δ)2[11]，根据预实验(n=151)结果，S=2.318，取α=0.05，Uα =1.96，允许误差(δ)为0.12，同时考虑20%失访率，计算所需样本量为1 791例。 调查方法 一般资料调查表 研究者自行设计一般资料调查问卷，问卷包括性别、年龄、婚姻、人事关系、工作年限、护士层级、职称、工作职责、夜班频率，以及是否接受过AI动态评估VTE风险培训等。 护士使用AI动态评估VTE风险接受度问卷 问卷由研究者以技术接受模型为理论框架自行编制。对11名VTE护理专家进行2轮函询，根据函询结果修订问卷内容。2轮专家函询中，有效问卷回收率均为100%，专家的权威系数为0.918，变异系数为0.115~0.327，肯德尔和谐系数分别为0.325、0.328(P<0.001)。最终形成的问卷包括4个维度、14个条目，分别为感知有用性维度(4个条目)、感知易用性维度(4个条目)、对AI信任度维度(3个条目)及使用意愿维度(3个条目)；采用Likert 5级计分法，每个条目从非常不同意至非常同意计分为1~5，总分为14~70，得分越高表示接受度越高。采用探索性因子分析检验问卷结构：Kaiser-Meyer-Olkin(KMO)值为0.924，Bartlett球形检验P<0.001，表明数据适合进行因子分析，累计方差贡献率为72.38%，各条目因子载荷为0.610~0.840，共同度范围为0.512~0.843，均大于0.500，表明各条目与所属公因子关系密切；采用验证性因子分析进一步检验量表的结构效度，基于修正指数并结合量表理论结构，对模型进行了适当修正。修正后模型的拟合结果显示：χ 2=119.656，自由度(df)=65，χ 2/df=1.841，比较拟合指数=0.971，拟合优度指数=0.900，近似误差均方根=0.075。综合各项拟合指标，模型与数据适配良好，符合结构方程模型拟合标准，表明量表具有良好的结构效度。本研究量表总体克龙巴赫α系数为0.865，各维度克龙巴赫α系数介于0.866至0.870之间，均达到0.700以上标准，提示量表整体及各维度条目内部一致性可靠。 临床护士预防住院患者VTE行为量表 临床护士预防住院患者VTE行为量表由杨梅等[12]编制，该量表包括知识、行为、态度3个维度共31个条目。采用Likert 5级评分法，从“非常不同意”赋值为1分至“总是或完全掌握”赋值为5分。知识维度总分为11~55，分数越高表明护士对预防VTE相关知识的掌握越好；行为维度总分为7~35，分数越高表明护士落实VTE预防行为的规范性越强；态度维度总分为13~65，分数越高表明护士对VTE预防的重视程度越高。本研究量表总体克龙巴赫α系数为0.863，各维度克龙巴赫α系数范围为0.851~0.869。 护士职业态度量表 护士职业态度量表由Rossiter等[13]编制，张帆等[14]进行翻译汉化。该量表包括职业认知、态度、意向3个维度，共29个条目。采用Likert 5级评分法从“非常不同意”至“非常同意”分别赋值1~5分，总分为29~145，得分越高表示护士的护理职业态度越好。本研究量表的总体克龙巴赫α系数为0.853，各维度克龙巴赫α系数范围为0.854~0.858。 资料收集及质量控制 采用电子问卷方式进行资料收集。研究前期，研究者提前与各医院护理部主任沟通，征得同意并获得研究支持后，由护理部主任将问卷链接下发至各相关科室护士长，研究者对参与问卷发放的科室护士长开展统一培训，随后各护士长组织科室符合纳入标准的护士自愿填写问卷。问卷首页明确研究目的、数据用途及保密承诺，调查对象确认知情同意后作答。问卷填写采取匿名设计、必答题设置、单IP地址单次作答限制。共发放问卷2 500份，为保障问卷质量剔除填写时间<3 min、规律作答的问卷，回收有效问卷2 323份。 统计学处理 采用SPSS 26.0统计学软件进行数据分析，符合正态分布的计量资料采用均数±标准差表示，多组间比较采用单因素方差分析；计数资料采用频数(构成比)表示，组间比较采用χ 2检验。采用Mplus 8.3软件建立潜在剖面模型。相较于传统的聚类分析，LPA是基于模型拟合的以个体为中心的分析方法，能够通过概率模型客观确定分类数量，避免主观设定类别数的偏差；同时LPA可提供多种拟合指数作为类别选择的客观依据，且在处理连续变量时更为稳健[10]。模型拟合的评价指标如下。1)信息评价指标：通过赤池信息量准则(Akaike information criterion，AIC)、贝叶斯信息准则(Bayesian information criterion，BIC)、样本校正的BIC(adjusted BIC，aBIC)，即3个指标数值越小代表模型拟合效果越好。2)分类评价指标：通过信息熵评估分类的精准性，取值为0~1，越接近1，表明分类精准性越高。3)似然比检验：通过罗-梦戴尔-鲁本校正似然比检验(Lo-Mendell-Rubin likelihood ratio test，LMRT)和基于Bootstrap的似然比检验(bootstrapped likelihood ratio test，BLRT)比较k个和k-1个类别模型间的拟合优度差异，当P<0.05时则前者最优[15]。本研究对各个模型结果进行综合判断，确定最佳模型。采用多元Logistic回归分析评估各因素对不同接受度类别的影响，检验水准α=0.05。 结 果 title: Perceived Healthcare Discrimination and Its Impact on Mistrust and Delayed Care Among Sexual and Gender Minority Young Adults in Spain
creator: Andrea Miranda-Tena, Francisco J. Sanmartín, Judith Velasco
description: Sexual and gender minority (SGM) individuals face discrimination in health care, compromising both well-being and access to services. Such experiences may foster expectations of mistreatment and mistrust of health care professionals, contributing to delays in care with potentially adverse consequences.

title: Health effects associated with alcohol consumption: a Burden of Proof study
creator: Xiaochen Dai, Sneha I. Nicholson, Hilary R. Lawlor, Sinclair Carr, Jaimie D. Steinmetz, Natalie M. Chen, Susan A. McLaughlin, Simon I. Hay, Kanyin L. Ong, Aleksandr Y. Aravkin, Peng Zheng, Reed J. D. Sorensen, Nora M. Gilbertson, Erin C. Mullany, Erin M. O’Connell, Christopher J. L. Murray, Emmanuel
description: A peer-reviewed research article from Europe PMC (2026). The relationship between alcohol and health is complex, and the evidence relating alcohol consumption to various cardiovascular diseases, cancers and other conditions is evolving. Moreover, alcohol drinking guidelines vary widely. Here we conducted 16 systematic reviews across four databases and conservatively re-evaluated dose–response relationships between alcohol consumption and 20 health outcomes, analysing 843 cohort and case–control studies using the Burden of Proof meta-analytic framework.

title: Advanced three-dimensional culture technologies in reproductive medicine: A narrative review
creator: Annahita Ghaedrahmati, Mohammad Zandi
description: A peer-reviewed research article from Europe PMC (2026). Recent advancements in 3-dimensional (3D) in vitro culture systems for follicles, oocytes, and embryos represent a paradigm shift in assisted reproductive technologies and reproductive biology. By mimicking the native physiological microenvironment more faithfully than conventional 2-dimensional systems, these innovative platforms directly address critical limitations of current in vitro embryo production protocols, including low blastocyst development rates, compromised embryo quality, and concerning epigenetic aberrations.

title: The Bacterial, Viral, and Microbiome Contributions in Cardiovascular Diseases: A Narrative Review
creator: Shyamala Ravikoti, Vikas Bhatia, Mohanasundari Saykkulandai Kuppuswamy
description: Cardiovascular diseases (CVDs) are the leading cause of morbidity and mortality worldwide. title: GPER介导的大气细颗粒物致肺癌作用研究进展
creator: Zhenhua LI, Dingbiao LI
description: 肺癌是全球癌症相关死亡的首要原因，大气细颗粒物（fine particulate matter, PM2.5）已被列为I类人类致癌物，大量流行病学证明其与肺癌发生发展存在紧密联系。G蛋白偶联雌激素受体（G protein-coupled estrogen receptor, GPER）近年来被发现可被多种环境污染物激活并诱发肿瘤，且在肺癌组织中显著高表达，揭示其在肺癌进展中扮演重要角色。研究发现，PM2.5中的环境雌激素类组分、金属离子等可激活GPER，进而调控丝裂原活化蛋白激酶/细胞外信号调节激酶（mitogen-activated protein kinase/extracellular signal-regulated kinase, MAPK/ERK）、磷脂酰肌醇3-激酶/蛋白激酶B（phosphoinositide 3-kinase/protein kinase B, PI3K/AKT）等下游信号通路，诱导炎症反应、氧化应激反应和铁死亡，最终影响肿瘤细胞增殖、凋亡、迁移、上皮-间质转化，重塑肿瘤微环境，共同驱动肺癌的发生和恶性进展。总之，GPER作为连接PM2.5环境暴露与肺癌恶性进展的关键分子枢纽，是极具潜力的干预靶点，靶向GPER的抑制剂有望为肺癌防治提供新策略。Keywords: 肺肿瘤, G蛋白偶联雌激素受体, 大气细颗粒物, 呼吸系统 肺癌是全球范围内发病率和死亡率最高的恶性肿瘤之一。统计数据[1,2]显示，肺癌发病数和死亡数分别占全球癌症总数的37.0%和39.8%，其中非小细胞肺癌（non-small cell lung cancer, NSCLC）占大多数。我国肺癌的发病率和死亡率均位居恶性肿瘤首位，是严重威胁公众健康的重要因素。研究[3,4]显示，2016年空气污染已成为仅次于吸烟致肺部非传染性疾病的第二风险因素，且在东南亚地区或成为肺癌最大病因，而大气细颗粒物（fine particulate matter, PM2.5）作为空气污染的主要成分，已被国际癌症研究机构列为I类人类致癌物，引起广泛关注。流行病学研究[5]表明，PM2.5暴露与肺癌风险、肺癌死亡率显著相关，其风险比（relative risk, RR）分别为1.16、1.23。随着工业化进程加速，人们越来越意识到PM2.5污染已成为全球重大的公共卫生挑战。G蛋白偶联雌激素受体（G protein-coupled estrogen receptor, GPER），又称G蛋白偶联受体30（G protein-coupled receptor 30, GPR30），作为一种新型膜受体，在肺癌组织中显著高表达，且与肿瘤分期晚、分化程度差密切相关[6]。近年来发现GPER能够介导多种环境污染物的雌激素样效应，导致人体内分泌与代谢紊乱，调节DNA损伤，诱发包括癌症在内的多种疾病，因此其也被称作“内分泌扰乱物受体”[7,8]。PM2.5中的雌激素样组分可能激活GPER，通过多途径驱动内环境改变促进肺癌发展。本文旨在系统综述GPER在PM2.5致肺癌中的作用机制，重点探讨其与PM2.5组分的交互网络、下游信号通路及肿瘤微环境重塑功能，为靶向GPER的肺癌防治策略提供新视角。 1 GPER的生物学特性及其在肺癌中的病理生理学作用 GPER是一种7次跨膜GPR，其基因位于染色体7p22.

title: 术前应用靶向药物治疗ALK阳性NSCLC患者的围手术期安全性分析
creator: Mengying FAN, Cunwei QIN, Yifan FANG, Hao FU, Liang DAI, Yongbo YANG, Zhen LIANG, Hongchao XIONG, Wanpu YAN, Keneng CHEN
description: 背景与目的局部晚期非小细胞肺癌（non-small cell lung cancer, NSCLC）的围手术期治疗一直是临床难点。虽然间变性淋巴瘤激酶-酪氨酸激酶抑制剂（anaplastic lymphoma kinase-tyrosine kinase inhibitors, ALK-TKIs）在ALK阳性NSCLC的术后辅助治疗中已确立重要地位，但其在术前新辅助治疗中的应用证据仍较匮乏。ALNEO等探索性研究提示术前ALK-TKIs治疗可带来比较理想的主要病理缓解（major pathological response, MPR）率，但围手术期安全性的临床报道依然有限。本研究旨在通过回顾性分析单中心数据评估术前ALK-TKIs治疗的围手术期安全性与可行性。方法回顾性分析2021至2024年北京大学肿瘤医院胸外一科前瞻性数据库中记录的接受术前ALK-TKIs靶向治疗并完成手术切除的ALK阳性NSCLC患者资料，评估其近期疗效、手术相关指标、围手术期并发症及远期生存情况。结果全组共11例患者，以女性并不吸烟患者为主（9/11），病理类型均为腺癌。治疗前临床分期为IIIA期7例、IIIB期3例、IV期寡转移1例。全组患者术前均接受ALK-TKIs治疗，其中4例联合化疗。客观缓解率（objective response rate, ORR）为81.8%。所有患者均顺利完成胸腔镜或机器人辅助手术，平均手术时间为（122.0±62.3）min，中位术中出血量74.0 mL（范围：5.0-300.0 mL）。MPR率为45.5%（5/11），病理完全缓解（pathological complete response, pCR）率为27.3%（3/11）。所有患者术后均接受了以靶向治疗为主的辅助治疗。中位随访30个月，全组无死亡病例，3例患者出现复发转移，其中1例为肠和肝转移，2例为脑转移。结论在本小样本队列中ALK阳性的NSCLC患者接受术前ALK-TKIs治疗显示出较好的安全性和可行性。Keywords: 肺肿瘤, 新辅助靶向治疗, 间变性淋巴瘤激酶, 安全性 肺癌仍是全球发病率与死亡率最高的恶性肿瘤之一，初诊即为局部晚期的患者，如可切除的N2/III期非小细胞肺癌（non-small cell lung cancer, NSCLC），是临床治疗上的难点[1]。对于此类患者，传统治疗策略强调多学科综合治疗，术前治疗是最受关注的一部分[2]，原因在于术前治疗（或新辅助治疗）可在手术前期控制微转移灶、缩小肿瘤体积、提高R0切除率，并为后续治疗策略提供“在体”疗效评估结果[3]。 随着精准治疗时代的到来，NSCLC的术前治疗日益强调以生物标志物为核心的个体化策略。程序性死亡配体1（programmed death-ligand 1, PD-L1）表达水平以及驱动基因如表皮生长因子受体（epidermal growth factor receptor, EGFR）、间变性淋巴瘤激酶（anaplastic lymphoma kinase, ALK）基因突变等，常用于甄别免疫治疗、化疗与靶向治疗的获益人群。对于ALK基因融合突变（ALK突变）的患者，术后辅助治疗领域目前推荐使用ALK-酪氨酸激酶抑制剂（tyrosine kinase inhibitors, TKIs）[4,5]；然而，目前支持ALK-TKIs用于术前治疗的证据相对匮乏，近年来仅有ALNEO[6]与LORIN[7]等探索性研究初步提示：将ALK-TKIs用于术前治疗能带来较为理想的影像与病理学的缓解，为这类人群的围手术期治疗提供了新的希望。 真实世界中在评估是否将ALK-TKIs用于术前治疗时，除了关注疾病缓解、肿瘤降期与R0切除等获益之外，还必须面对一个数据更少但同等重要的问题，即安全性，尤其是围手术期的安全，具体而言，如ALK-TKIs相关的不良反应及其是否导致剂量调整，治疗后组织水肿、纤维化及粘连对手术操作的影响，以及术前治疗是否会增加手术并发症、延长胸管留置及住院时间。这些关键的安全性问题均可能影响到临床决策。由于ALK基因突变概率较低，接受术前治疗者更为稀缺，因此目前关于安全性数据的报道仍然较少。 基于上述临床空白，本课题组开展了本项回顾性研究，旨在填补ALK-TKIs在术前治疗领域关于围手术期安全性的证据缺口，研究的假设是ALK-TKIs用于术前治疗并不会增加患者的不良事件（adverse events, AEs），不会影响后续的手术治疗。 1 资料与方法 1.1 临床资料 本研究回顾性分析了2021至2024年北京大学肿瘤医院胸外一科前瞻性数据库中连续性术前接受了ALK-TKIs治疗的NSCLC患者，对其围手术期安全性、近期疗效及远期生存情况进行分析。入组标准：（1）病理证实为NSCLC；（2）临床分期为III期及以上；（3）基因检测提示ALK突变阳性[免疫组化、荧光原位杂交（fluorescence in situ hybridization, FISH）或下一代测序（next-generation sequencing, NGS）]；（4）术前接受了ALK-TKIs靶向治疗者。排除标准：（1）未接受手术治疗；（2）术前未接受靶向治疗。本研究已获得北京大学肿瘤医院伦理委员会批准（No.2023KT86）。 1.

title: From Genes to Function: Clinical Experience with the Effectiveness and Safety of Risdiplam and Nusinersen in Spinal Muscular Atrophy
creator: Parinaz Sedighi, Afshin Fayyazi, Firozeh Hosseini, Kiana Karimi, Hossein Esfahani, Seyyed Mohammad Mahdi Hosseiny
description: Objective:Spinal muscular atrophy (SMA) involves the survival motor neuron (SMN) 1 gene, leading to motor neuron degeneration. SMN2 is a homologous gene to SMN1, which can produce SMN protein at lower levels. The new gene-based drugs modify SMN2 pre-messenger RNA splicing, leading to production of functional SMN protein.

title: Neurocutaneous Melanosis and Dandy-Walker Malformation in a Newborn: A Case Report
creator: Negin Armide, Bita Pourmohammadi, Meisam Babaei
description: Neurocutaneous melanosis (NCM) and Dandy-Walker malformation (DWM) are both uncommon congenital condition, involving the central nervous system (CNS). Combined NCM with DWM have been reported in a few studies. Potential consequences, including hydrocephalus and CNS malignancies make these illnesses extremely challenging to diagnose and treat.

title: Symposia
creator: Unknown
description: he tremor. Knowledge about the pathophysiology of tremor is relevant, because it helps to understand clinical heterogeneity (e.g., in the response to treatment) and because it aids the development of new, mechanism‐guided therapies. Here, I will discuss the pathophysiology of the most common tremor syndromes, including Parkinson's tremor, essential tremor, and dystonic tremor.

title: P18 Synergistic enhancement of chlorhexidine activity by Polyols against polymicrobial oral biofilms
creator: Hero Mohammed, Ayesha Rahman, Malgorzata Wiench
description: BackgroundBiofilm-associated antimicrobial tolerance is increasingly recognized as a driver of treatment failure and a contributor to antimicrobial resistance (AMR). Oral polymicrobial biofilms, implicated in dental caries and periodontal disease, exhibit intrinsic tolerance to antiseptics through extracellular polymeric substance (EPS) matrix protection, metabolic heterogeneity, and adaptive stress responses.

title: Characterizing Physical Therapy for Children and Adolescents Diagnosed with Concussion
creator: Anne Lennon, Mariann Strenk
description: Background:Physical therapy (PT) is a readily utilized treatment for individuals presenting with dysfunction after concussion. The American Physical Therapy Association (APTA) developed evidence-based clinical practice guidelines (CPG) for physical therapy management after concussion. While the CPG was published nearly five years ago, routine PT management for concussed youth has not subsequently been described.

title: P02 Assessment of tedizolid susceptibility against a collection of MRSA and VRE in comparison with linezolid
creator: Bharat Chandra Das, Md Nizam Ahmed, Madhavi Kirti, Aarsi, Parul Singh, Purva Mathur
description: BackgroundMDR Gram-positive bacterial infections remain a major therapeutic challenge in high-acuity trauma settings. MRSA and VRE are frequent causes of skin and soft tissue infections, nosocomial infections and bacteraemia. The emergence of linezolid resistance has further restricted available options.ObjectiveTo evaluate the susceptibility of tedizolid, a newer oxazolidinone, against VRE and MRSA isolates. Data from India regarding its efficacy is lacking.

title: From images to maps: a pipeline for creating synthetic electroanatomic mapping data
creator: A Von Kietzell, V Vigneswaran, K Maciunas, N Bodagh, M Klis, A Gharaviri, A Chiribiri, N Grubb, S Haldar, M O'neill, M O Bernabeu, S E Williams
description: BackgroundElectroanatomic mapping (EAM) generates detailed spatial and temporal datasets describing cardiac anatomy and electrophysiological function [1]. Despite their value, EAM data are rarely stored in electronic health records or shared between centres. Available datasets are typically small, fragmented, and difficult to combine due to technical heterogeneity and privacy constraints.

title: Machine learning based prediction models for outcomes following pulsed field ablation in atrial fibrillation
creator: A Saglietto, R De Lucia, M Magnocavallo, C Tondo, F Solimene, A Rossillo, M Bertini, S Themistoclakis, I Meynet, M Russo, A Dello Russo, V Velcich, M Malacrida, M Anselmino, G Zucchelli
description: BackgroundCatheter ablation is the most effective strategy for maintaining sinus rhythm in atrial fibrillation (AF); however, it is currently offered to only a minority of eligible patients. To optimize procedural benefit and cost-effectiveness, identifying candidates with the highest likelihood of long-term success is crucial.

title: Lesion characteristics after atrial fibrillation ablation using pulsed field ablation
creator: M Foti, L Bianchini, V De Sanctis, A Sanzo, M Casula, G Zingarini, R Maggio, L Rossi, F Tundo, A Dello Russo, S Bianchi, S Themistoclakis, S Iacopino, C Tondo, R Rordorf
description: Backgroundpulsed-field ablation (PFA) technology offers a non-thermal approach that is potentially more selective and safer than traditional techniques, but the extent of lesions and the unintentional involvement of the left atrial (LA) posterior wall (PW) remains unclear.PurposeThis study aimed to characterize PFA lesion formation following PVI in real-world atrial fibrillation (AF) patients using high-density (HD) voltage mapping.

title: P07 Beyond Mycobacterium ulcerans: secondary bacteria contribute to antimicrobial resistance in Buruli ulcer treatment
creator: Yaa Yeboaa Asare, Jennifer Morgan, Sandra Benin, Susana Debrah, Mabel Sarpong Duah, Charles Quaye, Lydia Mosi
description: Background and objectivesBuruli ulcer (BU) is a skin necrotizing disease caused by Mycobacterium ulcerans. It is characterized by painless lesions and treatment is by antimycobacterial agents. Previously, it was believed that mycolactone, the main virulence factor of the bacteria was highly bactericidal rendering other bacteria unable to survive in the lesions.

title: A Preregistered, Prospective, Longitudinal Examination of the Impact of Self-Initiated Sexual Orientation Change Efforts on Health and Changes in Sexuality
creator: G. Tyler Lefevor, Christopher H. Rosik, A. Lee Beckstead, Ty R. Mansfield, Mark A. Yarhouse
description: Although sexual orientation change efforts are generally understood to be ineffective and health-undermining, this understanding is based almost entirely on retrospective, cross-sectional data. We present prospective, longitudinal data from a sample of 315 sexual minority current/former members of the Church of Jesus Christ of Latter-day Saints to examine the efficacy and impact of self-initiated sexual orientation change efforts (SISOCE).

title: Long-term psychosocial and socioeconomic outcomes after living kidney donation: a single-center Romanian cohort study
creator: Lucas-Gabriel Discălicău, Cătălin Baston, Oana Moldoveanu, Alexandru Iordache, Teodor Căluşi, David Arnăutu, Ioanel Sinescu
description: A peer-reviewed research article from Europe PMC (2026). Living kidney donation is the treatment of choice for patients with end-stage kidney disease, yet the long-term psychosocial and socioeconomic consequences for donors remain incompletely characterized, particularly in Eastern European cohorts. This study aimed to assess the long-term psychosocial and socioeconomic impact of living kidney donation in a single-center Romanian cohort and to compare donor-reported outcomes by kidney function at last follow-up.

title: Autoimmune thyroiditis in pregnancy: epidemiology, clinical impact, and contemporary management challenges
creator: Alina Potorac, Octavian Munteanu, Alexandru Baros, Elena Evelina Stoica, Monica Mihaela Cirstoiu
description: Autoimmune thyroiditis represents the most common cause of thyroid dysfunction in women of reproductive age and is frequently encountered during pregnancy. The presence of thyroid autoantibodies, particularly anti-thyroid peroxidase antibodies, has been associated with adverse obstetric outcomes even in the absence of overt thyroid dysfunction. However, optimal screening, monitoring, and treatment strategies remain areas of ongoing debate.

title: Comparative cone beam computed tomography analysis of root canal morphology in permanent maxillary and mandibular canines within a Saudi Arabian subpopulation in the Albaha region
creator: Mohammed Sarhan Alzahrani
description: A peer-reviewed research article from Europe PMC (2026). The successful outcome of endodontic therapy is intrinsically linked to a comprehensive understanding of root canal anatomy and its frequent variations. The objective of this study was to evaluate the root and root canal morphology of permanent maxillary and mandibular canines in a Saudi subpopulation from the Al-Baha region using cone-beam computed tomography (CBCT), specifically investigating the prevalence of Vertucci classifications and canal shape variations across different root levels. This retrospective study analyzed 120 CBCT scans of permanent canines.

title: A Descriptive Assessment of Healthcare Workers' Preparedness for Digital Health Systems in Malawi
creator: Mayamiko Nkoloma, Harry Gombachika, Chomora Mikeka, Alfred Maluwa
description: IntroductionAlthough Malawi has expanded various digital health initiatives under its National Digital Health Strategy, there is still limited research on how prepared frontline healthcare workers really are to adopt and use Digital Health Systems (DHS). Most previous studies have focused on system level improvements in data reporting rather than on the experiences and preparedness of the users themselves.

title: Bibliometric Analysis of Pulmonary Fibrosis Imaging Research: Knowledge Graph Construction Based on the Web of Science Core Database
creator: Shuo Yu, Zhiyue Li, Yuting Zhang, Yaqi Yan, Min Tian, Yuhan Bian, Pardis Bahadori, Chenwang Jin
description: AimTo quantify publication trends, map international collaboration networks, and identify dominant and emerging research themes in Pulmonary fibrosis(PF) imaging (2015–2024).MethodsA structured Web of Science search combining PF- and imaging-related terms yielded 1,159 English-language original research articles. Analyses employed CiteSpace, VOSviewer, and Scimago Graphica for trend assessment, keyword co-occurrence, citation burst detection, and collaboration network visualization.

title: Society for Maternal‐Fetal Medicine Statement: Acetaminophen use during pregnancy
creator: Society for Maternal‐Fetal Medicine (SMFM), SMFM Publications Committee
description: A peer-reviewed research article from Europe PMC (2026). Acetaminophen has long been considered safe to use during pregnancy. A growing body of cohort studies and meta‐analyses has explored the potential association between prenatal acetaminophen use and neurodevelopmental outcomes in children. Although some studies report modestly increased risks of neurodevelopmental disorders in children exposed to acetaminophen prenatally, these findings must be interpreted with caution, given the inherent limitations of observational studies that may significantly affect the validity of the observed associations.

title: Safety and feasibility of leadless pacemaker implantation in elderly small-framed asian patients: a multicenter retrospective study
creator: M Asami, Y Enomoto, J Yamamoto, T Shimizu, N Sahara, N Nemoto, K Nakamura, H Hara
description: BackgroundLeadless pacemaker (LPM) therapy eliminates pocket- and lead-related complications of transvenous systems, however its large delivery sheath may raise safety concerns in small-framed elderly Asian patients. Data in this population remain scarce.AimTo assess the procedural safety, feasibility, and short-term outcomes of LPM implantation in elderly Asian patients, and to compare them with transvenous single-chamber pacemakers (TV-PM).

title: P12 Investigating the dynamic interaction between Salmonella and intestinal microbiota in health and disease
creator: Asmaa T Alenazi, Anjam Khan, Christopher Nile, Chien-Yi Chang
description: BackgroundAntimicrobial resistance (AMR) is an increasing global concern. The spread of MDR Salmonella enterica strains has limited the effectiveness of many commonly used antibiotics for treating gut infections, creating a clear need for alternative ways to reduce pathogen colonization and control infections.

title: P75 Vibrio cholerae bacteraemia in an immunocompetent returning traveller
creator: Sachika Paththamperuma, Linda Loterh, Madhuri Vidwans
description: Background Vibrio cholerae is a Gram-negative, comma-shaped bacterium that causes cholera, an acute diarrhoeal illness that remains endemic in many parts of Africa and South Asia. While it is well recognized as a cause of severe diarrhoeal disease, V. cholerae bacteraemia is rare, particularly in immunocompetent individuals. We present a case of V. cholerae bacteraemia in an immunocompetent returning traveller.

title: Personalized computational modelling of the electrical response to cardiac resynchronization strategies
creator: S Gerrits, L L T I Held, K C Smits, W Huberts, F W Prinzen, M J M Cluitmans, J G L M Leurmans, J Lumens, S Pezzuto, U C Nguyen, R Meiburg
description: A peer-reviewed research article from Europe PMC (2026). BackgroundIn patients with dyssynchronous heart failure, cardiac resynchronization therapy (CRT) is the preferred treatment. As a more physiological alternative to biventricular pacing (BiVP), left bundle branch area pacing (LBBAP) and LBBAP optimized CRT (LOT-CRT) are gaining traction. While LBBAP may correct a pure proximal left bundle branch block, its electrical effects in the presence of intraventricular conduction disease (IVCD) and myocardial scar remain unclear.

title: Pilot survey among patients taking bromhexine prophylactically against influenza
creator: Vanyo Mitev, Violeta S. Dimitrova, Iva Miteva, Rumen Tiholov, Krasimir Marinov, Ani Miteva, Aleksander I. Lilov, Radoslav Bilyukov, Zornitsa Mihaylova, Nikolay Ishkitiev, Konstantin Tachkov, Tsanko Mondeshki
description: Background:The successful use of bromhexine hydrochloride (BRH) for COVID-19 prevention led us to apply the same method for flu prevention. The goal of this study is to observe whether BRH could protect people against influenza.Methods:This is noninterventional, observational, questionnaire-based survey.

title: Knowledge, attitudes, and practices toward screening of colorectal cancer among adults in Kuwait primary health care centers
creator: Mahmood Alawainati, Sara N. Alshtaily, Rawan A. Almutairi, Aisha Alshammari, Ghalla Alotaibi, Sarah Kh. Alrashidi, Salma Alotaibi, Lujain Alotaibi, Eissa Althefairi, Khaled Alsubaiei
description: Background:The prevalence of colorectal cancer has been increasing both globally and in Kuwait. Early identification and treatment are essential to reduce its morbidity and mortality. This study aimed to assess the knowledge, attitudes, and practices toward screening of colorectal cancer among adults in Kuwait.Methods:A cross-sectional study was conducted across six governorates in Kuwait, including patients aged 18 years and above.

title: Constant ovulation during oral contraceptive treatment: Follicle-stimulating hormone-secreting pituitary adenoma case report and literature review
creator: Yang Yang, Lin Qiao, Jing Zhang
description: Follicle-stimulating hormone (FSH)-producing pituitary neuroendocrine tumor is very rare and usually present with menstrual disorders, ovarian cysts, polycystic ovary morphology (PCOM), and so on. It is often confused with polycystic ovary syndrome (PCOS) and is difficult to diagnose. Missed or misdiagnosis may lead to unnecessary surgical injury or severe neurologic damage.

title: Perspectives of mothers regarding infant swaddling and hip health in Riyadh, Saudi Arabia: Behavioral trends and associated determinants
creator: Hays S. Alfawaz, Rana A. Alhazzani, Abdulrhman A. Almazrou, Alhassna Alkahmous, Nourah A. Alkahmous, Omar A. Alkahmous, Aram Aldughayyim, Shatha Y. Asiri, Mastourah A. Alshahrani, Sarah A. Alessa, Ameerah S. Assiry, Khulood Y. Almaddi, Abdulelah F. Alshehri
description: Background:Infant swaddling that restricts physiological hip flexion and abduction has been identified as a modifiable postnatal risk factor for developmental dysplasia of the hip (DDH). Despite increasing biomechanical evidence linking improper swaddling techniques to adverse hip development, caregiver-related determinants of hip-safe swaddling practices remain insufficiently characterized in Middle Eastern populations.

title: The Relationship of Micro and Macro Worries on the Acceptability of Corruption: The Role of Basic Human Values
creator: Ekaterina V. Maklasova, Alexander N. Tatarko, Klaus Boehnke
description: BackgroundCorruption severely threatens societal stability and well-being, with various factors contributing to its prevalence. This study, relying on theory and empirical research on the relationship between suffering and fraud, offers a new explanation, that worries may be an essential factor in the acceptability of corruption. People’s worries are the consequences of suffering they experience throughout their lives.

title: Low Brain Levels of Dietary Polyphenols and Their Conjugates: Reassessing Mechanisms of Alzheimer’s Disease Prevention
creator: Roshni Sharma, Kristina Shkirkova, William J. Mack, Rayudu Gopalakrishna
description: Dietary polyphenols such as quercetin, resveratrol, and (−)-epigallocatechin-3-gallate (EGCG) have shown neuroprotective effects in epidemiologic and experimental studies of Alzheimer’s disease (AD), although clinical evidence remains limited. This review highlights the importance of investigating glucuronide and sulfate conjugates of these polyphenols, as well as their intestinal microbial metabolites, at bioavailable low nanomolar concentrations, particularly those capable of reaching the brain.

title: Data Resource Profile: Device-measured physical activity and sleep in the HUNT4 study, Norway
creator: Vegar Rangul, Atle Kongsvold, Saraswoti Lamsal Khanal, Mats Flaaten, Eivind Schjelderup Skarpsno, Kerstin Bach, Tom Ivar Lund Nilsen, Paul Jarle Mork
description: ata from ∼230 000 individuals. The Trøndelag Health Study (HUNT), initiated in 1984–6 in mid-Norway, is a population-based study with four consecutive surveys among adults (HUNT1–4, ≥20 years) and adolescents (Young-HUNT1–4, 13–19 years) that comprises health data from ∼230 000 individuals.

title: Peak-frequency mapping in detecting atrial ganglionated plexi in patients with functional bradycardia
creator: T Kamakura, T Ikee, D Shako, S Oka, A Wakamiya, N Ueda, K Nakajima, K Nakasuka, M Wada, K Ishibashi, Y Inoue, K Miyamoto, T Aiba, K Kusano
description: A peer-reviewed research article from Europe PMC (2026). BackgroundStandardised methods for the identification of ganglionated plexi (GP) are lacking. Peak-frequency (PF) mapping may serve as an effective approach for identifying atrial GP sites with fractionated potentials. Atrial GP detection has been indicated within a region characterised by high PF (≥600 Hz) in patients with functional bradycardia; however, the detailed anatomical associations between high PF regions and atrial GP-positive sites are yet to be established.PurposeIn this study, we evaluated the use of PF mapping for the detection of atrial GP.MethodsWe evaluated

title: P69 A cross-sectional audit of antibiotic utilization and AWaRe stewardship alignment in hospitalized patients
creator: S Harshitha, Afrin Siddique, Angel Jennifer, D Suresh Kumar
description: BackgroundAntibiotic utilization audits are well established in high-income settings but remain limited in developing healthcare systems, where the burden of antimicrobial resistance is high and stewardship practices are still evolving. Prescribing is often empirical, with variable adherence to evidence-based principles.

title: More Than Activity: The Effect of Sustained Engagement in Digital Alcohol Support Interventions for Regional and Remote Communities
creator: Katinka van de Ven, Getenet Dessie, Kedir Y. Ahmed, Nicole Lee, Hazel Dalton, Julaine Allan, Subash Thapa
description: PurposeThis study examines differences between major city and regional and remote participants in engagement in a digital alcohol support intervention (Daybreak), risky drinking, and psychological distress and tests the mediating role of psychological distress.MethodsThis was a longitudinal, observational cohort study of Daybreak participants between January 2019 and December 2024 (N = 12,824). Outcomes were risky drinking and psychological distress.

title: When Scientific Reassessment Fails Citizen Science. Comment on Soldo, A. When Citizen Science Becomes Speculation: Evaluating the Reliability of Lamnid Shark Identification from Photographic Records in the Mediterranean. J. Mar. Sci. Eng. 2026, 14, 173
creator: Patrick L. Jambura, Julia Türtscher, Joshua K. Moyer, Kenshu Shimada, Ilija Ćetković, Branko Dragičević, Pero Ugarković, Mišo Pavičić, Phillip C. Sternes, Simone Niedermüller, Jacopo Bernardi, Matteo Barbato, Frederik H. Mollen, Jürgen Kriwet, Douglas J. Long, Taketeru Tomita, Charlie J. Underwood,
description: Soldo [1] raises concerns about the reliability of citizen science-derived photographic records for identifying lamnid sharks in the Mediterranean Sea. Using a recently published juvenile white shark from Croatian waters [2] as a representative case, the author reinterprets the specimen as a porbeagle shark (Lamna nasus) rather than a white shark (Carcharodon carcharias), based primarily on selected dental characters.

title: Understanding barriers to treatment regimen adherence in Pakistani women with polycystic ovary syndrome: a cross sectional study
creator: Moeza Zulfiqar, Waqas Akram, Muhammad Talha, Muhammad Zulnurain, Emaan Saif, Ali Akhtar
description: BackgroundPolycystic ovary syndrome is a prevalent endocrine disorder among reproductive-age women, significantly impacting their quality of life and increasing the risk of chronic diseases.ObjectivesThis study aimed to determine adherence levels and main barriers to adherence to prescribed treatment regimens among women with PCOS in Lahore, Pakistan.

title: Cohort Profile: The North East London Diabetes Study (NELDS)
creator: Abraham Olvera-Barrios, Alasdair N Warwick, Matilda Pitt, Zeinab Schaefer, Schanhave Santhirasekaran, Ryan Chambers, Louis Bolter, John Anderson, Jiri Fajtl, Sarah Barman, Reecha Sofat, Aroon Hingorani, Catherine Egan, Adnan Tufail, Alicja R Rudnicka, Christopher G Owen, Nayani G Adhikari, Nayani G
description: jtl, Aaron Lee, Abraham Olvera-Barrios, Christopher G Owen, Paolo Remagnino, Alicja R Rudnicka, Royce D Shakespeare, Adnan Tufail, Charlotte Wahlich, Alasdair N Warwick, Roshan Welikala Published: 2026 The North East London Diabetes Study (NELDS) was established to investigate the epidemiology of diabetes-related outcomes and to support the development of equitable predictive models.

title: The long crisis of Italy’s National Health Service: universalism on paper, inequity in practice
creator: Nicola Abrescia, Adelaide Maddaloni, Gabriella Molinaro, Antonio Capponi, Maurizio D’Abbraccio
description: nal: patients may retain legal entitlement to care while being forced to wait, travel considerable distances, or pay privately to obtain it. The crisis is therefore not the disappearance of rights, but the weakening of the public system’s capacity to make those rights effective.

title: P77 Burden of MDR pathogens in hospitalized patients: a clinical microbiology study
creator: Greta Lila, Rezarta Bajrami, Yllka Begolli
description: ObjectivesMDR organisms (MDROs) pose a growing threat in healthcare settings. Transmission and persistence of the resistant strain is determined by the availability of vulnerable patients, selective pressure exerted by antimicrobial use, increased potential for transmission from larger numbers of colonized or infected patients (‘colonization pressure’) and the impact of implementation and adherence to prevention efforts.

title: P28 Antimicrobial activity of imipenem/relebactam and comparators against clinical Gram-negative bacilli collected in the UK: results from the Study for Monitoring Antimicrobial Resistance Trends (SMART) 2020–24
creator: M Wise, M Allen, F Siddiqui, K Young, M Motyl, D Sahm
description: BackgroundImipenem/relebactam (IMI/REL) is a combination of the carbapenem, imipenem, with the β-lactamase inhibitor relebactam, an inhibitor of Class A & C β-lactamases. IMI/REL is approved in the UK and EU for adults with hospital-acquired and ventilator-associated bacterial pneumonia, as well as complicated urinary tract and complicated intra-abdominal infections.

title: Evolução dos desfechos cirúrgicos em metástases vertebrais de tumores sólidos: Análise comparativa ao longo de 2 décadas *
creator: Fernando Pacheco dos Santos Ferreira da Silva, Pedro Reggiani Anzuatégui, Ana Valéria Rigolino Teixeira, Fernanda Pinto Garcia, Lucas Emanuel Sauer Larocca, Glauco José Pauka Mello
description: ResumoObjetivoAvaliar a evolução dos desfechos cirúrgicos em pacientes submetidos à cirurgia para metástases vertebrais de tumores sólidos ao longo de mais de duas décadas em um único serviço terciário.MétodosEstudo retrospectivo comparativo envolvendo 2 coortes de pacientes submetidos a tratamento cirúrgico para metástases vertebrais: coorte 1 (2002–2015) e coorte 2 (2018–2024).

title: Predictions and cross-center validation of IDH status and 1p/19q status in adult diffuse glioma with non-invasive magnetic resonance spectroscopy
creator: Zhangren Tu, Wanjun Hu, Jialve Zhang, Zhen Xing, Jiamin Li, Jingjing Xu, Meijin Lin, Xianwang Jiang, Dairong Cao, Jing Zhang, Di Guo, Xiaobo Qu
description: This study developed and validated a non-invasive multi-metabolite magnetic resonance spectroscopy framework for preoperative molecular subtyping of adult diffuse gliomas. Using a cross-center, cross-vendor cohort of 268 patients, 48 features derived from 18 metabolites were systematically evaluated to identify discriminative metabolic signatures for predicting IDH mutation and 1p/19q codeletion status.

title: Primary care-based interventions for post-stroke follow-up for long-term care: a systematic review
creator: Hannah Ravenhall, Serena Sabatini, Rhiannon De Ivey, Linda Errington, Khalifa Mohammed, Rachael Raw, Emily Symington, Faye Tabone, Jacob Brain, Eugene Yee Hing Tang
description: BackgroundLife after stroke is managed by primary care to prevent recurrent stroke and ensure that stroke survivors live well within the community. Unfortunately, stroke survivors do not always receive timely follow-up from clinical services, which leads to unaddressed and hidden unmet needs.

title: Rural Health Workforce Development Through the AHEC Scholars Model
creator: Danielle Bruno, Taylor O'Shaughnessy, Jennifer D. Taylor
description: IntroductionIt is widely understood that access to health care services is crucial to achieving and maintaining good health. The Indiana AHEC Scholars program was developed to help combat these shortages by providing post‐secondary health professions students with a didactic curriculum paired with community‐based rural and/or medically underserved experiences in local communities.

title: Recruiting Rural Patients for Clinical Research: Lessons From a Colorectal Cancer Screening Trial
creator: Gina A Keppel, Brooke Ike, C Holly A Andrilla, Allison M Cole
description: PurposeThe Colonoscopy Outreach for Rural Communities (CORC) study is a randomized controlled trial testing the effectiveness of a remotely‐delivered patient navigation program to increase colonoscopy completion for colorectal cancer (CRC) screening among rural and underserved patients. This study assesses CORC's success in recruiting rural patients and outlines approaches for including rural residents in clinical research.

title: Palliative care in humanitarian responses
creator: Hanna Kaade, Felix Muehlensiepen, William E Rosa, Martin Heinze, Marcel Kamp, Matthew J Allsop
description: A peer-reviewed research article from Europe PMC (2026). mong people with serious chronic and progressive conditions when treatment is interrupted and access to care is disrupted, fragmented or lost. Pain, breathlessness, anxiety, depression and functional loss are common after sustained injury in armed conflict, disasters and displacement.

title: A model for the epidemiological impact of tuberculosis policy options
creator: Sandip Mandal, Srinath Satyanarayana, Finn McQuaid, Peter J Dodd, Nicolas A Menzies, Richard G White, Nimalan Arinaminpathy, Rein MGJ Houben, David W Dowdy, Mikaela Smit, Suvanand Sahu, Carel Pretorius
description: A peer-reviewed research article from Europe PMC (2026). ObjectiveTo develop a new tuberculosis transmission model, addressing the limitations of and building on the TB Impact Model and Estimates software tool, to enable decision-makers to assess the impact of various tuberculosis interventions and allocate resources more effectively.MethodsWe designed a model incorporating diagnosis and treatment pathways across public and private sectors, stratified across age groups, drug susceptibility, human immunodeficiency virus status and vaccination status.

title: Translating WHO theory on alcohol to practice—where are we in the policy spectrum?
creator: Avi Magid
description: ealth policy in terms of guidelines and recommendations. Furthermore, some European countries have already recommended a total avoidance of alcohol consumption [2]. The manner in which this risk assessment should be translated into policy is a matter of ongoing debate forming a policy spectrum that ranges from informed individual decision-making to a rigid collective-centred precautionary approach.

title: Environmental sustainability evidence in critical care medicine: a scoping review
creator: Marko Balan, Thomas Bodley, Kiyan Heybati, Jiawen Deng, Melany Gaetani, Christina Maratta, Michelle Swab, Karen E A Burns, Srinivas Murthy
description: A peer-reviewed research article from Europe PMC (2026). PurposeWe sought to conduct a scoping review to summarize the existing literature on environmental sustainability in critical care medicine, methods for measuring intensive care unit (ICU)-related environmental impact, and interventions to improve ICU environmental sustainability.SourceWe conducted a systematic search of four databases to identify studies published before October 2024 pertaining to environmental sustainability and assessment of the carbon footprint of ICUs and manually screened selected journals.Principle findingsThe combined search strategy identified 1,967 potentially eligible articles.

title: Measuring vision loss beyond blindness: a severity transition in an ageing world
creator: Henry Bair
description: read as a public-health success. Yet a steep fall at the most severe end of the spectrum, alongside little movement at the moderate end, is the pattern expected under a particular kind of change. Legacy blindness-centred metrics, and even newer effective-coverage indicators, are not designed to show how many years of life are lived in each severity state.

title: From guidelines to practice: general practitioners' consensus on indicators for managing selected multimorbidity in primary care in Western Australia
creator: Sage M C Ishimwe, Timothy A Carey, Jacquita S Affandi, Ninh Thi Ha, Amna Mushtaq, Sayyida Anees, Christopher M Reid, Dan Xu, Delia Hendrie
description: A peer-reviewed research article from Europe PMC (2026). BackgroundMultimorbidity is rising in primary care, yet adherence to guidelines is hindered by fragmented, disease-specific recommendations. This study sought to establish consensus among general practitioners (GPs) on indicators of adherence to Australian guidelines in managing five common chronic conditions [type 2 diabetes mellitus (T2DM), obesity, hypertension, cardiovascular disease, and chronic kidney disease (CKD)], aiming to develop a unified tool for holistic care.MethodsA two-round reactive Delphi survey was conducted with 21 GPs in Western Australia, following RAND methodology.

title: Metabolomics of per- and polyfluoroalkyl substances (PFAS) exposure: Advances in LC-MS technology and applications
creator: Yu-Meng Wang, Pei-Chen Lin, Yu-Da Zheng, Pin-Shiuan Wu, Kuo-Tai Hua, Sung-Fang Chen
description: Per- and polyfluoroalkyl substances (PFAS) are a class of synthetic chemicals known for their high stability and bioaccumulation potential, leading to their widespread presence in the environment and human tissues. Exposure to PFAS has been associated with significant health concerns, including neurotoxicity, hepatotoxicity, and metabolic disturbances.

title: The evolution of DESI-MSI: A comprehensive look at preprocessing and quantification strategies for metabolomics
creator: Cheng-Hung Yang, Hung-Yao Ho, Chen-Yu Chang, Mei-Ling Cheng
description: Mass spectrometry imaging (MSI) has become an indispensable tool in metabolomics for visualizing the spatial distribution of biomolecules within tissues. Due to its direct, ambient analysis capability, desorption electrospray ionization (DESI-MSI) has evolved from a rapid screening tool into a precise and reliable quantitative platform.

title: The protective potential of intestinal Bifidobacterium-derived extracellular vesicles with unique lipid composition against blue light-induced damage in retinal cells
creator: Wei-Hsuan Hsu, Pin-Hsuan Su, Hao-Yuan Chien, Tzu-Ming Pan, Bao-Hong Lee
description: Bifidobacterium longum is a probiotic that resides in the intestine, and extracellular vesicles (EVs) released by microorganisms have garnered attention in recent years for their role in regulating host health. This study found that triacylglycerol, cholesteryl esters, and free fatty acid (18:0 and 16:0) are primarily composed of lipids in B. longum-derived EVs by lipidomics assay.

title: EvoSubster: a pipeline for evolutionary inference of single- and double-base substitution spectra
creator: Mariko Nakagawa, Martin C Frith
description: MotivationMutational processes differ widely across the tree of life, yet most existing resources focus on somatic mutations in humans or on a limited set of well-studied species.ResultsWe present EvoSubster, a simple and extensible pipeline for inferring evolutionary single-base and double-base substitution spectra from closely related species using a parsimony-based three-genome comparison.

title: Survival as a source of confounding, selection bias, and effect modification
creator: C Mary Schooling, Guoyi Yang
description: BackgroundSurvival is a long-standing source of confounding, selection bias, and effect modification that is often overlooked. Here, we describe how it can occur and when it can be averted.MethodsDirected acyclic graphs were used to illustrate how survival could cause confounding and selection bias.

title: The impact of improved air quality on low birth weight and health inequalities in Spain from 2010 to 2018
creator: Stefan Sieber, Joan Ballester, Mark Nieuwenhuijsen, Andrea Pozzer, Cathryn Tonne
description: BackgroundWe aimed to estimate the association of air pollution and term low birth weight (LBW) by maternal education and assess the distributional impact of meeting European Union and World Health Organization air pollution targets and universal tertiary maternal education on LBW cases.

title: A machine learning approach to identify at-risk populations for yellow fever vaccination
creator: Madison Farnsworth, Kostiantyn Botnar, Justin T Nguyen, Riley K Watson, Trevor L Murphy, Susan LF McLellan, Kamil Khanipov, George Golovko
description: A peer-reviewed research article from Europe PMC (2026). Introduction:Vaccinations play a crucial role in public and personal health. Vaccines such as the Yellow Fever 17D vaccine are effective at preventing disease and provide lifelong immunity with few adverse events. Leveraging the increase in electronic medical records and the widespread use of machine learning algorithms in healthcare, this study aims to investigate and develop an algorithmic framework for analyzing clinical data on Yellow Fever 17D vaccinations in order to predict at-risk populations for adverse events following immunizations.

title: Epilepsy and amygdalar enlargement: cause or consequence?
creator: Cristian Hardaman, Luis Ariel Miquelini, Federico Sánchez González, Juliana Belvel Fernandes Lastoria, Yemina Soledad Neme Segura, Ignacio Lagger, Oscar Martínez
description: The amygdala is a central structure of the limbic system. For several decades, volumetric asymmetries of the amygdala have been described, initially associated with psychiatric disorders. In epilepsy, a growing literature highlights the distinctive features of amygdala enlargement (AE), considering that since its original description, diagnosis has been primarily radiological.

title: MRI-based study of gray matter volume and cortical morphological alterations in patients with rheumatoid arthritis
creator: Mingqing Xu, Shipin Zang, Yifan Yang, Ru Bai, Shuang Liu, Ruomei Cui, Shu Li, Yuqi Cheng, Jian Xu
description: ObjectiveTo investigate alterations in gray matter volume (GMV) and cortical morphology in patients with rheumatoid arthritis (RA) and examine their associations with clinical characteristics using voxel-based morphometry (VBM) and surface-based morphometry (SBM).Methods41 RA patients and 34 age- and sex-matched healthy controls (HCs) underwent high-resolution structural magnetic resonance imaging (sMRI).

title: Evaluation of the United States’ Permitless Concealed Carry Laws and Child Health in the ECHO Cohort
creator: Marie L. ChurchilL, Emily A. Knapp, Alexander D. Mccourt, Nandita Somayaji, Courtney K. Blackwell, Lyndsay A. Avalos, Kelly A. Hirko, Kaja Z. Lewinn, Johnnye Lewis, Yeyi Zhu, Alison E. Hipwell, Margaret R. Karagas, Kristen Lyall, Jody M. Ganiban, Nigel Paneth, T. Michael O’shea, Christine C. Johnson
description: A peer-reviewed research article from Europe PMC (2026). Firearms are the leading cause of death among children in the United States (US). As of 2023, half of US states had enacted laws allowing permitless concealed carry of firearms. Our cross-sectional study evaluated the association between permitless concealed carry laws and child general health using data from the nationwide Environmental influences on Child Health Outcomes (ECHO) Cohort collected between 2003 and 2023. Children aged 1–21 years with caregiver- or self-reported general health status were included.

title: Association of severe maternal morbidity with epilepsy diagnosis in children: a population-based birth cohort study
creator: Bénédicte Driollet, Emmalin Buajitti, Asma M Ahmed, Jennifer A Hutcheon, Laura Rosella, Seungmi Yang
description: A peer-reviewed research article from Europe PMC (2026). BackgroundSevere maternal morbidity (SMM) is associated with adverse perinatal outcomes. However, its association with longer-term offspring outcomes, including neurodevelopment disorders, is poorly understood. This study aims to examine the association between SMM and the risk of epilepsy in offspring.MethodsA retrospective birth cohort study of all singleton hospital births between 2002 and 2018 in Ontario, Canada was followed up until March 2020.

title: A large randomized trial assessing alcohol cessation versus moderation on clinical events: UNATI
creator: Miguel Ángel Martínez-González, María Barbería-Latasa, María Barbería-Latasa, Zenaida Vázquez-Ruiz, Miguel Angel Alvarez-Mon, Diego Martínez-Urbistondo, Miguel Ruiz-Canela, Maira Bes-Rastrollo, Miguel A. Martínez-González, Jesús Antonio Vaquero-Cruzado, Javier Quintero, Albert Bellvert, Maria Teresa
description: The health effects of moderate alcohol consumption remain a highly debated topic in public health and epidemiology. While observational studies have suggested a possible protective effect of moderate drinking, particularly within Mediterranean patterns, concerns about confounding and selection bias persist. No randomized trial to date has definitively addressed whether alcohol cessation offers superior health benefits compared to sustained moderate drinking.

title: Correlation of pulse oximetry with arterial blood gas–derived oxygen saturation in ICU patients on supplemental oxygen: a cross-sectional study
creator: Bikash Pandey, Birendra Jha, Sumit Shahi, Shital Adhikari
description: Introduction:Oxygen is essential for maintaining proper bodily functions and is closely regulated within the body. Hypoxemic patients, who have lower than normal oxygen levels in their blood, require precise monitoring to ensure appropriate oxygen therapy. Arterial blood gas (ABG) analysis (SaO2) and pulse oximetry (SpO2) and are two widely used methods to assess oxygen saturation of hemoglobin in blood.

title: Five-Year Immune Recovery After ART Initiation Among PLWH Aged ≥15 Years with Baseline Immunosuppression — China, 2013–2024
creator: Yunxia Geng, Hanlu Jia, Yuan Guan, Ruiqi Ren, Decai Zhao, Xiumin Gan, Lieyu Huang, Nana Liu, Zhihang Peng, Yan Zhao
description: IntroductionAlthough antiretroviral therapy (ART) suppresses human immunodeficiency virus (HIV) replication in most people living with HIV (PLWH), 10%–40% show inadequate CD4 reconstitution despite sustained virologic suppression, increasing risks of AIDS- and non-AIDS-related events. Prior studies have suggested that immunological nonresponse (INR) is particularly common among individuals starting ART with immunosuppression.

title: Mysterious cohabitation with socially assistive robots among three underserved groups
creator: Othelia EunKyoung Lee, Sojeong Baek, Do-Hyung Park
description: Background and ObjectivesThis study investigates how underserved individuals—older adults, low-income middle-aged men, and adults with disabilities—develop long-term relationships with an AI-powered socially assistive robot (SAR) named Hyodol. We examined how these relationships evolve over eight months and why emotional outcomes differ across three groups.

title: Contributions of preeclampsia to preterm delivery: a hypothetical interventional cohort study using incremental propensity scores
creator: Wen Wei Loh, Cande V Ananth
description: A peer-reviewed research article from Europe PMC (2026). BackgroundPreeclampsia remains a leading cause of preterm delivery (PTD). Conventional average causal effect estimands may not always be perfectly suited for assessing preeclampsia’s contributions because they rely on uniform counterfactual scenarios, such as everyone suffering from preeclampsia.

title: The abnormal C-terminus caused by DVL1 variants impacts Robinow syndrome phenotypes
creator: Shruti S Tophkhane, Gamze Akarsu, Sarah J Gignac, Xinyi Xie, Katherine Fu, Esther M Verheyen, Joy M Richman
description: Robinow Syndrome is a genetically heterogeneous, rare skeletal disorder characterized by craniofacial and limb defects. All 7 causative genes lie in the Wingless-related Integration site-1 (WNT) pathway. Here we study the pathogenesis of DVL1 (Dishevelled 1), the most commonly affected gene, where variants cause a frameshift that replaces the C terminus with a novel peptide.

title: Purine and Pyrrolopyrimidine‐Based Small Molecules as Multitarget Therapeutics
creator: Federica Borghi, Antonio Laus, Claudia Sorbi, Giulio Rastelli
description: Purines and pyrrolo[2,3‐d]pyrimidines are privileged heterocyclic scaffolds widely represented in small molecules targeting a broad range of therapeutically relevant targets, including kinases, folate‐metabolizing enzymes, histone deacetylases (HDACs), bromodomain containing proteins, membrane transporters, phosphodiesterases (PDEs), ion channels, and toll‐like receptors (TLRs).

title: Comparative study of the degradation of the 2,4-dichlorophenoxyacetic acid herbicide using zinc oxide and zinc oxide/graphene oxide photocatalysts: efficiency, stability, toxicity, kinetics and mechanism insights
creator: Ana Elizabeth Rodrigues de Freitas, Flaviano Henrique de Sousa Medeiros, João Pedro Gonçalves de Souza Soares, Marcos Gomes Ghislandi, Melissa Gurgel Adeodato Vieira, Vivian Stumpf Madeira, Mauricio Alves da Motta Sobrinho
description: A peer-reviewed research article from Europe PMC (2026). This study investigated the degradation of the herbicide 2,4-dichlorophenoxyacetic acid (2,4-D) in aqueous solution through heterogeneous photocatalysis under simulated solar irradiation. For this purpose, zinc oxide (ZnO), graphene oxide (GO), and a ZnO/GO composite were synthesized and characterized using Fourier-transform infrared spectroscopy (FTIR), X-ray diffraction (XRD), dynamic light scattering (DLS), scanning electron microscopy (SEM), energy-dispersive spectroscopy (EDS), diffuse reflectance spectroscopy (DRS), and photoluminescence (PL) analyses.

title: Ingested twin ball magnets in a Nepalese boy: swallowed but not forgotten!
creator: Ashish Lal Shrestha, Saukat Ali, Satyam Rimal Upadhyay
description: Introduction and importance:Swallowed foreign body in children is a common and frequent emergency, with most of them passing through the gut without complications. Ingesting multiple magnets or a magnet along with another metallic object, however, poses a significant risk to the bowel due to potential complications such as obstruction, pressure necrosis, perforation, and fistulation.

title: Qualitative perceptions of child and youth mental health services by caregivers in the WHO European Region: a systematic review of qualitative literature
creator: Tania Cardona, Katie H Atmore, Raffaella Sibilio, Jennifer Hall, Anastasia Giannaki, Penny Kalpaxi, Joao Breda, Ledia Lazeri, Tatiana Taylor Salisbury
description: A peer-reviewed research article from Europe PMC (2026). The rising prevalence of mental health conditions in children and young people requires responsive, high-quality care from child and adolescent mental health services (CAMHS) that consider the needs of service-users and their caregivers. This systematic review seeks to contribute evidence-based recommendations from caregivers’ perspectives to inform the development of quality standards for CAMHS in the World Health Organization (WHO) European Region.

title: Successful 10-year long-term follow-up after artificial dural patch suturing for iatrogenic dural defect created during spinal arachnoid cyst resection: a case report
creator: Dong-Ju Lim, Ju-Young Jung
description: Introduction and importance:Spinal arachnoid cysts (SACs) are rare intraspinal lesions containing cerebrospinal fluid (CSF). Symptomatic SACs require surgical decompression, but excision can be complicated by iatrogenic dural tears (incidental durotomy), which occur in 1–17% of spinal surgeries. Effective, watertight closure is critical to prevent CSF leakage, infection, and recurrence.

title: Well-Being Under Structural Constraints of Political Instability in the Israeli-Occupied West Bank: A Cross-Sectional Study
creator: Rula Ghandour, Abdullatif Husseini, Shiraz Nasr, Rita Giacaman
description: A peer-reviewed research article from Europe PMC (2026). The well-being of Palestinians living under prolonged Israeli occupation is deeply conditioned by the structures of deprivation and control that shape daily life. Using data from 3,000 adults residing in refugee camps and surrounding urban areas of the West Bank, this study examines how deprivation, political violence, and human rights violations relate to well-being as measured by the World Health Organization-Five Well-Being Index. Nearly three-quarters of respondents (73.8%) reported poor wellbeing.

title: Improving Effective Prenatal Care for New Obstetric Patients Using a Standardized Intake Template and Pregnancy Risk Calculator
creator: Morgan De Kleine, Sharanna S Johnson, Kaya S. Belknap
description: IntroductionKenya has the 16th highest maternal mortality rate and the 58th highest infant mortality rate in the world. Most of these deaths are preventable and attributed to inadequate prenatal care. A chart audit at Africa Inland Church Kijabe Hospital revealed significant gaps in care at the initial prenatal visit.

title: Exploring oxidative stress and epigenetic biomarkers in bees: insights into health effects of air pollution and diet – a pilot study
creator: Roberta Giorgione, Marcello Messi, Daniela Pigini, Maria Luisa Astolfi
description: A peer-reviewed research article from Europe PMC (2026). Bees are vulnerable to environmental pollution, including toxic emissions from fire events, which can impact oxidative balance. This study was conducted as a pilot investigation with a relatively limited sample size and aimed to assess the levels of specific biomarkers [8-oxo-7,8-dihydroguanine (8-oxoGua), 8-oxo-7,8-dihydroguanosine (8-oxoGuo), 8-oxo-2′-deoxyguanosine (8-oxodGuo), 3-nitrotyrosine (3-NO₂Tyr), and 5-methylcytidine (5-MeCyt)] by HPLC‒MS/MS analysis in bees sampled before (May) and after (June) a landfill fire. The bees were divided into three groups: untreated (control), supplemented with Quassia amara, or fed probiotics.

title: Perceived physical exertion in senior workers performing heavy manual tasks
creator: Albin Stjernbrandt, Pontus Öhrner, Andreas Tornevi, Jerry Öhlin, Farhad Abtahi, Charlotte Lewis, Mikael Forsman, Viktoria Wahlström
description: With an aging workforce and longer working lives, staying in physically demanding occupations is increasingly challenging, and the factors influencing perceived exertion are still poorly understood. Also, self-rated exertion may not correlate strongly with physiological measurements of physical strain at work, such as heart rate.

title: Tracing spatial mid-size Eastern U.S. cities road dust pollution: insights from source apportionment and health risk assessment
creator: Minh Tri Truong, Chattan T. Haselden, Anh-Chi Tuan, Justin B. Richardson
description: As urban areas expand in eastern USA, the convergence of historical and modern anthropogenic source inputs has resulted in a complex geochemical signature of road dust pollution, while representing a critical public health issue for communities. In this study, road dust collected at seven (7) cities in eastern USA was analyzed for 11 potential toxic elements (PTEs, e.g.

title: 1,2,3‐Triazole‐Linked Chalcones as Privileged Scaffolds in Anticancer Agents
creator: Sumeyya Koldas, Guler Yagiz Erdemir, Ahsen Kilic, Neslisah Barlak, Omer Faruk Karatas, Aliye Altundas
description: A new series of extended‐functionality triazole‐substituted chalcone derivatives was synthesized, and their in vitro anti‐proliferative and cytotoxic profiles were evaluated using cancer and non‐cancer cell models. First, all compounds were screened in the FaDu head and neck squamous cell carcinoma cell line to identify the most active candidates with comparatively lower IC50 values.

title: Statistical Inference in Database Exploitation: Sample Size and Confounding Factors
creator: Carmen Carazo-Díaz, Luis Prieto-Valiente, Carmen Carazo-Díaz, Luis Prieto-Valiente
description: Database (DB) exploitation is an essential tool in medical and epidemiological research, enabling the extraction of hidden insights from large volumes of information through statistical analysis. This work provides a methodological reflection on two critical aspects of such studies, namely sample size and confounder detection via multivariate analysis.

title: The Dual Role of VEGF in Intracerebral Haemorrhage: From Pathological Mechanisms to Therapeutic Opportunities
creator: Yunlian Niu, Xiaoqian Wang, Yichen Huang, Xuemei Zhang, Yijie You, Peiyuan Ding, Fengbing Sun, Jian Zhang
description: An intracerebral haemorrhage (ICH) is a general type of haemorrhage in the brain, which arises due to the rupture of cerebral blood vessels. Many molecules have been investigated for their potential ability to modify hemostasis and blood-brain barrier function in ICH. Vascular endothelial growth factor (VEGF) is highly expressed in some diseases and helps induce angiogenesis.

title: Antimicrobial Susceptibility of Human Pasteurella multocida Isolates in Korea, 2022–2025
creator: Hye Gyung Bae, Jae Han Sohn, Hochan Seo, Byeonghak Kwak, Myungsook Kim, Jae-Seok Kim, Mi-Kyeong Lee, Kyungwon Lee
description: BackgroundPasteurella multocida is an important zoonotic pathogen that causes soft-tissue infections in humans; however, recent antimicrobial susceptibility data in Korea remain limited.Materials and MethodsA total of 70 clinical P. multocida isolates collected at a nationwide commercial laboratory in Korea between November 2022 and July 2025 were analyzed.

title: Survey on COVID-19 Vaccination among Pediatric Cancer Patients and Their Parents: A Single-Center Study from Korea
creator: Areum Shin, Doo Ri Kim, Hee Young Ju, Ji Won Lee, Keon Hee Yoo, Ki Woong Sung, Yae-Jean Kim
description: BackgroundImmunocompromised children are a high-risk group for severe coronavirus disease 2019 (COVID-19). A nationwide study in Korea found that the average COVID-19 vaccination rate in high-risk children was higher than in the general pediatric population, whereas vaccination rates in pediatric cancer patients were lower.

title: Epidemiology, clinical management, and outcomes in patients with eosinophilic granulomatosis with polyangiitis in England: A retrospective observational cohort study
creator: Salman Siddiqui, Bo Ding, Paul Dolin, Chris Edmonds, Priya Jain, Jennifer Rowell, Lotte Westerink, Alessandra Lacetera, Pablo Suárez-Sánchez, Cono Ariti, Bélène Podmore, Alvaro Kitchin Velarde, Stephanie Y. Chen
description: BackgroundData on the clinical burden of eosinophilic granulomatosis with polyangiitis (EGPA) are limited.ObjectiveWe sought to evaluate the epidemiology and clinical burden of EGPA in England using real-world evidence.MethodsPatients diagnosed with EGPA between January 1, 2006, and February 28, 2019, who had ≥1 year of data before diagnosis (index date) were identified using the Clinical Practice Research Datalink Aurum database.

title: Perceptions of death, dying and the body in Vietnamese culture: A qualitative exploration from a study examining the potentials of minimally invasive tissue sampling in Vietnam
creator: Nhung Phuong Doan, My Nguyen Le Thao, An Luu Phuoc, Alix Day, Halina Suwalowska, Ho Dang Trung Nghia, Mary Chambers, Ta Thi Dieu Ngan, H. Rogier van Doorn, Jennifer Ilo Van Nuil
description: BackgroundPerceptions of death and dying has been attracting more attention in recent years with more advocacy on improving the end-of-life experiences and providing more support for families during these times. While these topics are important, Western views about death and dying have been more dominant, leaving a knowledge gap in how death and dying are perceived in Asian cultures.

title: An evaluation of the US public–private Combating Antibiotic-Resistant Bacteria Accelerator (CARB-X) initiative
creator: Rena M Conti, Mathew Alexander, Eric J Evans
description: A peer-reviewed research article from Europe PMC (2026). IntroductionDeveloping novel antibiotics to replace ineffective existing ones is a priority policy objective. The Combating Antibiotic-Resistant Bacteria Accelerator (CARB-X) is the largest global public–private initiative to advance this goal. The US-based CARB-X has committed over $1 billion US dollars through 2028 to innovators, and provides financial and technical support for the development of novel antibiotics through a competitive request for proposal application process.MethodsWe evaluated the outcomes of all applications to CARB-X between the program's inception in 2016 through 2019.

title: Deferred prescribing in practice: an observational study in community pharmacies in France during 2024–5 and feedback from pharmacists
creator: Justine Coudière, Céline Mongaret, Samuel Adelou, Bénédicte Pereton, Hélène Vaillant-Roussel, Amélie Richard
description: BackgroundExcessive use of antibiotics promotes antibiotic resistance. Deferred prescribing (prescriptions dispensed according to clinical progress) is a strategy to reduce this overconsumption. Recognized in some countries, this practice is poorly documented and not recommended in France.ObjectivesTo determine the rate of deferred outpatient prescriptions, their dispensing rate, and their characteristics.

title: From Retigabine to Azetukalner: Reviving Voltage‐Gated Potassium Channels for Epilepsy Therapy
creator: Pascal Rosendahl, Lukas Schulig, Andreas Link
description: A peer-reviewed research article from Europe PMC (2026). Heterotetrameric KV7.2/3 potassium channels were retrospectively identified as the target of the analgesic flupirtine and the antiepileptic retigabine (ezogabine). Clinical utility of these agents ended after decades or 6 years, respectively, before their full scope was explored. Market withdrawals in 2017 and 2018 hampered research in other medical fields and left a gap for researchers using these compounds off‐label in experimental indications and for patients with KV7.2/3 malfunctions.

title: Molecular Mechanisms and Probe‐Dependent Effects of Clinically Relevant GABAA Receptor Modulators
creator: Marvin Taterra, Yuan Chang‐Halabi, Marcel Bermúdez
description: Modulators of γ‐aminobutyric acid type A (GABAA) receptor, including benzodiazepines, anaesthetics, and Z‐drugs, act through distinct allosteric mechanisms that remain incompletely understood at the molecular level. Here, we investigate probe‐dependent pharmacology in GABAA receptor modulation by integrating molecular dynamics simulations, deep learning‐based enhanced sampling, dynamic pharmacophores, and our recently developed MDPath approach for mapping allosteric communication networks.

title: Glomerulonephritis through the lens of ultrasound and radiology
creator: Guido Gembillo, Salvatore Silipigni, Concetto Sessa, Lorenzo Lo Cicero, Luca Soraci, Annalisa Cozza, Rocco Bruccoleri, Luigi Peritore, Walter Morale, Andrea Corsonello, Antonio Bottari, Domenico Santoro
description: Renal biopsy remains the diagnostic reference in glomerulonephritis, and no imaging modality has displaced its central role. The key question is whether imaging can complement histology by providing additional information on disease activity, prognosis, and treatment response. In clinical practice, conventional ultrasound is the first-line examination.

title: Post-transplant metabolic dysregulation: Insights and implications for kidney graft survival
creator: Tabassum Elahi, Saima Ahmed, Muhammed Mubarak
description: Kidney transplantation is the preferred treatment for end-stage kidney disease, improving survival and quality of life. Yet, metabolic disorders including post-transplant diabetes mellitus, dyslipidemia, hyperuricemia, secondary hyperparathyroidism, and obesity are common in kidney transplant recipients and threaten graft function and patient outcomes.

title: A curated list of InDel markers for rapid genetic mapping in Arabidopsis thaliana
creator: Fahad Mohammed Tonmoy Chowdhury, Koki Mutsuda, Taku Takahashi
description: Identification of novel functional genes through mutant analysis is one of the most powerful approaches in plant science. In the model plant Arabidopsis thaliana, this approach typically combines whole-genome sequencing of the mutant with fine mapping using molecular polymorphic markers between two ecotypes to narrow down the genomic region containing the mutant allele.

title: Identification of different cDNA clones of the Apomixis-specific gene-1 homolog involved in aposporous embryo sac formation in guineagrass (Panicum maximum Jacq.)
creator: Lanzhuang Chen, Liming Guan, Taiji Adachi
description: Apomixis is the reproduction mode in which only the mother’s genes are transmitted from generation to generation. If this trait can be put to practical use, it is expected to be a truly epoch-making breeding method, as seed production costs can be greatly reduced by fixing F1 hybrids.

title: Evaluation of bicuspid aortic valve-associated aortopathic changes using third-generation dual-source computed tomography
creator: Salai Thanihaivel E, Arun Sharma, Mansi Verma, Rajesh Vijayvergiya, Manphool Singhal
description: A peer-reviewed research article from Europe PMC (2026). Bicuspid aortic valve (BAV) affects 0.5%-2% of the population and is associated with progressive aortopathy leading to life-threatening complications. Aortic size index (ASI) adjusts aortic dimensions for body surface area (BSA), potentially improving risk stratification.AIMTo characterise BAV-associated aortopathic changes using third-generation dual-source computed tomography (CT) and to derive a cohort-specific ASI threshold associated with CT-defined ascending aortic dilatation in an Indian population.METHODSThis prospective cross-sectional study enrolled 100 BAV patients (age > 18 years) from July 2022 to November 2023.

title: Appendix in ulcerative colitis pathogenesis and therapy: An updated narrative review
creator: Omar AbdelGhani, Sherreen Elhariri, Payal Bhatnagar, Htar Htar Aung, Mohamed Abdel Wahab, Nabil Eid
description: A peer-reviewed research article from Europe PMC (2026). Ulcerative colitis (UC) is a chronic inflammatory disorder of the colon. Its pathogenesis has been linked to chronic intestinal inflammation stemming from genetic predisposition, immune dysregulation, changes in gut microbiome, and various environmental factors. There is emerging evidence for autophagy dysfunction in the UC setting, suggesting a compromise of the intestinal epithelial barrier and microbial clearance in patients, resulting in chronic activation of the immune system. There is growing evidence that the appendix functions as a critical priming site for UC.

title: The Effect of Rural Versus Urban Residence on Risk of Unplanned Readmission and Death in Older Veterans Discharged From VA Hospitals
creator: Joanne K. Daggy, Anthony J. Perkins, Katie Ross‐Driscoll, Laura J. Myers, Stanley E. Taylor, Mathew J. Reeves, Greg Arling, Indrakshi Roy, Scotte R. Hartronft, Cathy C. Schubert, Dawn M. Bravata
description: PurposeEvidence suggests that rural‐residing adults—compared with urban—may be at greater risk of readmission and mortality. Operational leaders within the Department of Veterans Affairs (VA) Geriatric Learning Health System (GLHS) sought to understand the effects of rural residence on readmission and mortality risk for older Veterans discharged from hospital to home.

title: An expanded cortical map of von Economo neurons in the human medial prefrontal cortex
creator: Daniela Ortiz-Muñoz, Carlos Arturo González-Acosta, Oscar Alonso Plaza-Patiño, Efraín Buriticá-Ramírez, Lina Vanessa Becerra-Hernández
description: Von Economo neurons (VENs) are large bipolar projection cells, confined to the anterior cingulate and frontoinsular cortices, yet their broader cortical distribution remains unresolved. Previously, we reported these neurons in the dorsomedial portion of cortical area 9 and polar-medial area 10.

title: Bacillus subtilis DnaB forms multiple protein–protein interactions essential for DNA replication initiation
creator: Aurélie Guyet, Reyes Ruiz Campoy, Petra Manja, Frederic D Schramm, Simone Pelliciari, Stepan Fenyk, Yuanyuan Li, Charles Winterhalter, Aravindan Ilangovan, Heath Murray
description: DNA replication is initiated at specific chromosomal loci termed origins.
